blindSummary: Research found no region-specific laws, incidents or enforcement patterns that differ from this country's national framework - the record adds nothing beyond the national picture.
blindSourceSummaries: Investigative feature (12 January 2018) on the plight of transgender women in this country's prisons: incarcerated on the basis of legal gender status, most trans women housed in all-male facilities because placement follows the sex on the ID document (a criminal-procedure provision separates men and women only); first-person accounts (a trans woman held in another facility in 2014, shouted at by other detainees; another foreign trans woman detained after a publicised 2016 protest trial in the capital); the national detention monitor says transgender detainees - the majority of whom are women - are the group that 'suffers the most' in prison.

Opinion of 25 May 2021 of the national detention monitor (unofficial translation) on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty: serious violations of fundamental rights persist across all detention settings, based on some forty referrals since 2010, interviews with trans associations and international experts, observations from the interior, justice and health ministries, and on-site and document inspections; recommendations extend to intersex and non-binary persons; follows an initial 2010 opinion on trans prisoners.

Torture-prevention organisation blog (edited interview with the national preventive mechanism): trans persons deprived of liberty face a constant risk of violence, discrimination and abuse; a new opinion (25 May 2021) was needed because the 2010 opinion covered only incarcerated trans persons and because detention conditions had not improved despite new gender-recognition laws; the new opinion extends to all places of deprivation of liberty and to intersex and non-binary people, based on a decade of letters from detained trans people, ministry and association input and exchanges with international experts.
